Save a results dashboard to share

Source: R/dashboard.R
export_dashboard.Rd

Saves a dashboard in one of two forms:

Usage

export_dashboard(
  x,
  path = NULL,
  ...,
  format = c("shiny", "html"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  open = interactive()
)

Arguments

x

a model, mv_model_selection object, or the app returned by mv_dashboard().

path

for format = "shiny", the folder to write (created if needed); for format = "html", the file to write (.html is added if missing). Defaults to "mirtverse-dashboard" or "mirtverse-dashboard.html".

...

arguments passed to mv_dashboard() when x is a model, such as panels, title or dif.

format

"shiny" for a deployable app folder or "html" for a single file that works offline.

overwrite

logical; replace an existing dashboard at path.

open

logical; for format = "html", open the file in a browser afterwards.

Value

The folder or file path, invisibly.

Details

  • format = "shiny" writes a folder with an app.R file and the dashboard summary (dashboard.rds). Run it locally with shiny::runApp(path), or publish the folder to shinyapps.io or Posit Connect with rsconnect::deployApp(path). The server installs mirtverse the way you installed it, so install it from GitHub or r-universe (not from a local folder) before you deploy.

  • format = "html" writes a single self-contained .html file that needs no server, no R and no internet connection: email it, put it on a shared drive or a course page, and it opens in any browser. It has the same panels, with the item table, item curves, ability slider and person lookup still interactive.

Neither form holds item responses. Individual scores are included only if the dashboard has the "persons" panel.

Examples

# \donttest{
mod <- mirt(Science, 1, verbose = FALSE)
dir <- export_dashboard(mod, file.path(tempdir(), "science-dashboard"),
                        title = "Science attitudes survey")
#> Drawing 4 item health cards...
list.files(dir)
#> [1] "app.R"         "dashboard.rds"
if (interactive()) shiny::runApp(dir)

f <- export_dashboard(mod, file.path(tempdir(), "science.html"), format = "html",
                      title = "Science attitudes survey")
#> Drawing 4 item health cards...
# }
